gap: No result ChatGPT got states the price per rated watt that each amp delivers into a single 4 Ω passive subwoofer when wired its strongest way: Behringer NX3000D $0.11/W when bridged, Crown XLS1002 $0.45/W bridged, Fosi Audio M03 $0.51/W, Dayton SPA250DSP $1.11/W.
standout_why: ChurchSoundCalc (churchsoundcalc.com/best/power-amplifiers-for-churches, opened 2026-11-10) gives only price ceilings and per-channel watts. It has no bridged ratings and no cost per watt. Its NX3000D row even shows 1,500 W at 4 Ω, which is Behringer's 2 Ω figure. ChatGPT cited two B&H compare pages, but both returned 403 to me, so I could not check whether they compute a cost per watt. As retailer spec grids they normally list ratings and price side by side without dividing them. I did not open the Sweetwater category pages; they are product lists with no single-sub arithmetic. None of the pages I could read covers the $50–$500 consumer subwoofer amps (Fosi M03, Dayton plate amp) together with the pro rack amps.
decides: For one 4 Ω passive sub, bridging the NX3000D gives about 4× more rated watts per dollar than any other candidate. That confirms ChatGPT's top pick on value. The Crown has to be bridged to compete, and used one channel at a time it costs $1.41/W. For a small sub that needs about 150 W or less, the Fosi M03 costs $76 in total against $278 for the Dayton plate amp and gives similar watts per dollar. The Dayton is the worst on this measure, and ChatGPT showed it at $411.99, while Amazon lists it at $277.98.
